The scan reads "تین سو تیرہ (300)" — the words say 313 while the numerals look like "300"; the commonly cited figure is 313 (the "313" dismissals of 1972). Transcribed as 313 with this note.
Printed sequence: the ordinance of 1972 is described before "16 جنوری 1972ء" (more units); the dates are kept as printed. The paragraph continues on page 5.
Historical note: the nationalisation of the banks is generally dated 1 January 1974 (Banks Nationalisation Act); the book prints "19 مئی 1972ء". Kept as printed.

Printed as "280 دفعات"; the 1973 Constitution as adopted has 280 articles — consistent. FATA was merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by the 25th Amendment (2018); the book's description reflects the original text.
Historical note: the Qadiani/Ahmadi community was declared non-Muslim by the Second Amendment (1974), not in the original 1973 text. Kept as printed.
Printed "مارچ 1978ء" for the Lahore High Court's death sentence on Bhutto; the verdict is usually dated 18 March 1978 — consistent.
Printed "پاکستان جنرل ضیاء الحق" at the top of the page continues "صدر" from page 12 ("صدرِ پاکستان جنرل ضیاء الحق").

The scan of this page is slightly slanted; the clause "the government could appeal against the decision of the Appellate Shariat Bench" is ambiguous as printed — it most likely means "could appeal (against a Shariat bench decision) to the Appellate Shariat Bench of the Supreme Court".
Printed error: "آئین کی دفعہ 298" — section 298-A is part of the Pakistan Penal Code (added by Ordinance XLIV of 1980), not of the Constitution. Kept as printed.
The Federal Ombudsman's term was four years under the 1983 order — consistent.
Historical note: the nominated Majlis-e-Shura (1981) had well over 50 members (initially about 288); the book prints "50". Kept as printed.

Missing source page: printed page 16 is absent from both the PDFs and the JPG folder (JPG "021_Page_015" is followed by "022_Page_017"). It evidently covered the end of the Zia-era Islamic measures and the start of the Afghan jihad section (the Soviet intervention of 1979 and Pakistan's support); not reconstructed. This page begins mid-sentence.
"پچاس ہزار روسی فوج" (fifty thousand Soviet troops) is printed without a verb; it probably means Soviet troop losses. Historical Soviet deaths were about 15,000. Kept as printed.

Printed date differs from page 12: there "20 مارچ 1985ء کو محمد خان جونیجو پاکستان کے وزیرِ اعظم بنے" (became PM on 20 March); here he was chosen on 20 March and sworn in on 23 March. Kept as printed.

Printed date inconsistency: page 12 says Zia announced the end of martial law on 30 December 1985; here it is lifted "from 1 January 1986" — both kept as printed (the announcement and the effective date).
Historical note: Zulfiqar Ali Magsi was Chief Minister of Balochistan 1993–96 and his government was not ended by the PPP in that period; the sentence is kept as printed.
Duplicate scan: 10th pakstudy2.pdf page 1 is identical to 10th pakstudy1.pdf page 31 (printed page 26, see p030).
Historical note: the military courts were set up by an ordinance of November 1998 (struck down in February 1999); the book's date "30 جنوری 1999ء" is kept as printed.
The printed name is "صدر محمد رفیق احمد تارڑ"; elsewhere (page 28) it is "محمد رفیق تارڑ". Kept as printed.
Printed inconsistency: the referendum is said to be both announced and held on "30 اپریل 2002ء"; historically it was announced on 5 April and held on 30 April 2002. Kept as printed.

Printed errors: "جو الیکشن کمیشن نے ... جاری کیے" attributes the President's orders to the Election Commission, and the emergency is dated "14 اگست 1999ء"; the emergency was proclaimed on 14 October 1999. Kept as printed.
The PML(Q) seat count "72" is as printed (it refers to the directly elected general seats announced on election night; final totals with reserved seats were higher).
Historical note: in Sindh the PML(Q)-led coalition governed, and in Balochistan the MMA shared power with PML(Q) in a coalition; kept as printed.
"آخری 8 سال" (last 8 years) — Musharraf ruled about 8–9 years in total; "6.8%" is an annual growth figure for 2002–07. Kept as printed.
Printed grammar: "زیادہ منافع کمانے کی چکر میں" (standard "کے چکر میں"). Kept as printed.
Printed content issue: "بالواسطہ ٹیکسوں کی جگہ بلاواسطہ ٹیکسوں" — the general sales tax listed just above is itself an indirect tax. Kept as printed.
Historical note: Musharraf was re-elected President by the outgoing assemblies (electoral college) in October 2007, not by a vote of confidence of the National Assembly. Kept as printed.
Answer (ii) follows the text on page 4, which dates the take-over of further industrial units to 16 January 1972 (the first ordinance is given only as "1972").
Q2(ii): the chapter gives no date for the Shariat benches; "1980" in the model answer is the historical date (Federal Shariat Court established May 1980).
Q3 asks for long essay answers; students should draw on pages 2–37 (sections 1-1 to 1-15). No single model answer is given.
The timeline table is not printed in the book; it is a study aid compiled only from dates given in this chapter (caretaker governments and acting presidents omitted).
The compass rose on the printed map shows "مشرق" (east) on the left and "مغرب" (west) on the right, i.e. reversed; the map itself is drawn with west on the left.
Printed "سیکیورٹی کونسل کی مستقل رکنیت بحال کرانے" — the PRC took China's UN and Security Council seat in 1971 (Resolution 2758). Kept as printed.
Printed "14 جولائی سے 17 جولائی 2001" is called "تین روزہ مذاکرات" (three-day talks); the Agra summit was held 14–16 July 2001. Kept as printed.
Printed "پاکستان اور ایران کے علاوہ چھ اور ترقی پذیر ممالک" — D-8 has eight members in total (i.e. six besides Pakistan and Iran); consistent. D-8 was formally established in 1997.
Historical note: Afghanistan was a kingdom in 1956 (King Zahir Shah; PM Daoud Khan visited Pakistan); "افغانستان کے صدر" is kept as printed.
Historical note: Pakistan recognised the Taliban government in May 1997 (with Saudi Arabia and the UAE), not "1996"; the sentence says it was the first — kept as printed.
Historical note: Turkmenistan declared independence in October 1991, so a gas agreement in "ستمبر 1991ء" predates it; kept as printed.
Historical note: Almaty was Kazakhstan's capital until 1997 (now Astana); the book's statement refers to 1994.
Printed "معاہدہ بغداد (CENTO) اور (SEATO) میں شمولیت" — Turkey was a member of the Baghdad Pact/CENTO but not of SEATO. Kept as printed.
Historical note: Azerbaijan declared independence in August 1991 (and Pakistan recognised it in December 1991); the book prints "اگست 1992ء". Kept as printed.
Duplicate scan: 10th pakstudy3.pdf page 1 is identical to 10th pakstudy2.pdf page 31 (printed page 56, see p061).
Historical note: Afghanistan joined SAARC in 2007; the founding members (1985) were seven. Kept as printed.

Printed claim that the US stopped arms supplies "supporting India" — in 1965 the US embargoed arms to both Pakistan and India. Historical note: Pakistan left SEATO in 1972–73 and CENTO in 1979. Kept as printed.
Printed page 61 (European Union, Japan, start of Russia) is bound out of order in 10thpakstudy4.pdf (page 11) and is transcribed as p103; this page continues its Russia paragraph.
The paragraph above continues the Russia section that begins on printed page 61 (p103).
The second UN resolution's date is printed "3 جنوری 1949" or "5 جنوری 1949" (the digit is unclear in the scan); the UNCIP resolution is dated 5 January 1949, which is used here.
Printed error: General Zia-ul-Haq addressed the UN General Assembly in 1980 as the OIC's representative but did not preside over it. Kept as printed.
Printed "عالمی تنظیم برائے خوراک (WFO)" — the UN food agencies are the FAO and WFP. Kept as printed.
Answer (xi): the chapter discusses five Central Asian republics (Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan) plus Azerbaijan; the standard count of Central Asian states is five.

Q3 asks for long essay answers; students should draw on pages 43–64 (sections 2-1 to 2-10). No single model answer is given. Relations with the EU, Japan and Russia (needed for 3(iv)) are on printed page 61, bound out of order (p103).
The organisations table is not printed in the book; it is a study aid compiled from this chapter's text.
"148 ٹن" of improved seed for the whole country looks too small (likely "148 ہزار ٹن"); kept as printed.
Note: this chapter dates bank nationalisation to 1974, whereas Chapter 1 (page 5) gives "19 مئی 1972ء"; 1974 is historically correct. Both kept as printed.
Khewra is in Jhelum district (Pind Dadan Khan tehsil); the caption "کھیوڑہ (جہلم)" is consistent.
"پیرکوہ" (Pirkoh) is in Dera Bugti, Balochistan, not Punjab; kept as printed.

Printed claims: "دنیا کا سب سے بڑا کوئلے کا ذخیرہ تھر" — Thar is among the world's largest lignite deposits, not the largest; Thar coal mining began in 2019. Kept as printed. The place names "سار شارگ ڈیگاری" are printed run together.
Printed "چنائی" for the Balochistan marble site; probably "چاغی" (Chagai). Kept as printed.
Printed claim "دریائے سندھ کا میدان دنیا میں سب سے زیادہ زرخیز علاقہ" is an overstatement; kept as printed.

Printed figures are inconsistent: 38% cultivable + "remaining 62%" treats 62% of the total area as also convertible; and "24 فی صد" is ambiguous (of the total area or of the cultivable land). Kept as printed.
Printed typo: "تباہ کاروں س کئی" for "تباہ کاریوں سے کئی"; corrected in transcription.
The sentence "زرعی تحقیق کی حوصلہ افزائی کرنا ہو گی تاکہ پیداوار بڑھائی جا سکے" is printed twice (under 4 and 5). Kept as printed.
"کالا باغ" here refers to the Kalabagh (Jinnah) Barrage on the Indus, not the proposed Kalabagh Dam.
Printed content: sorghum (jowar) is not normally an edible-oil crop and is not typical of the Hazara hills (the description fits maize); kept as printed.
Duplicate scan: 10thpakstudy4.pdf page 1 is identical to 10th pakstudy3.pdf page 31 (printed page 87, see p092).
Printed "مچھلی برآمد کر کے اور قیمتی زرِ مبادلہ کمایا جاتا ہے" — the sentence is partly printed on a pasted correction slip. Kept as read.
Figures (70% thermal / 30% hydro) reflect the book's period; kept as printed.
Printed grammar: "حکومتِ پاکستان ... خود کفیل ہو جائے گا" (masculine verb with feminine "حکومت"); kept as printed.
Printed "ملک صنعت میں" (probably "ملکی صنعت میں"); kept as printed.

Printed "ارنی لعل" — the Kashmiri poet is usually written "ارنی مال" (Arnimal); kept as printed.
